archetypes.name: test-crossref
archetypes.rationale: The plan names specific test case identifiers and assertion strings to rename/update across three test files; verify each exists at the described location and that no order-asserting cases are missed.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan names specific current test case identifiers (ci_fix_vendor_tier_order_cursor_first, run_ship_pr_2632_t4, t4b, t4c, t4d, and the BOOTSTRAP_MD/BOOTSTRAP_SH assertion strings) in scripts/test-ship-pr.sh, scripts/test-ship-pr-fix-loop-2632.inc.sh, and scripts/test-implement-step2-routing.sh — verify each current identifier actually exists in the file at the described location with the exact assertion strings the plan says to change. Check whether those files contain additional cursor/codex ordering assertions not mentioned in the plan that would also need updating to keep the harness green after the flip. Confirm the assert_not_contains guard for the 'Codex → Cursor → Claude' literal is present in test-implement-step2-routing.sh and that the plan's proposed comma-based SKILL.md wording would satisfy it without triggering a false positive. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: prose-drift
archetypes.rationale: The plan defers two named cursor-first surfaces (R1/R2) and updates eight named files; verify no additional cursor-first ordering prose exists in files outside that boundary that would be silently left stale.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan explicitly defers two surfaces as out of scope (R1: design plan-review Cursor-slot fallback in docs/review-agents.md and docs/collaborative-sketches.md; R2: brainstorm framing lane in skills/design/references/brainstorm.md) and lists eight files for update — search the broader codebase for 'Cursor → Codex', 'cursor.*codex', or 'cursor_first'-style ordering prose in files outside both lists to identify stale references the implementation would silently leave behind. Also verify the two deferred surface paths actually exist and contain the cursor-first patterns described in the report section, so the deferral claim is accurate. Check the sibling .md docs for each modified .sh script (per the script-md-siblings rule) to confirm the plan accounts for all doc-sync obligations introduced by the script changes. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
